features.description: Operator-editable caps file at ~/.jarvis/quota_caps.json. Schema: {schema_version: 1, defaults: {claude_tier}, <vendor>: {<tier>: {<window>: {cap, unit, _note?}}}}. NOT in repo (lives in ~/.jarvis/, outside the tree). NOT reusing dashboard/state/costs.json (different audience: app-level GCP $-spend vs per-vendor agent quota — see feedback_operator_config_separation.md). Sibling subcommands on `python -m jarvis_orchestrate`: `quota-caps init [--overwrite]` writes a starter file (samples current Codex rolling_5h via _codex_usage_v2 to derive cap = ceil(observed * 1.25); falls back to high provisional 1B tokens if no sample; refuses to overwrite without flag); `quota-caps show` reads + validates the file and prints effective caps. Starter caps (post F006a fix#2): claude.max_20x.rolling_7d cap=100 unit=percent_of_plan with _note flagging the F006 uncalibrated-skip requirement AND telling the operator how to extend coverage to rolling_5h (rolling_5h is intentionally NOT seeded — each percent_of_plan cap requires its own dashboard sample, weekly bar vs session bar, so dual-seeding would force two calibrations before first dispatch could clear); codex.plus.rolling_5h unit=tokens_local_proxy (NOT messages_estimate — F006 compares against observed_native which is tokens, so messages_estimate would silently false-trip); gemini.code_assist_individuals.rolling_24h cap=1000 unit=requests; grok={} (empty until F003 detects a real signal). Loader validates schema_version + KNOWN_VENDORS/TIERS/WINDOWS/UNITS at load-time; rejects unknowns with named-key errors. Validator rejects cap <= 0 (F006a fix#2 — was cap < 0; aligned with evaluate_window's defensive cap_value <= 0 check). Permits underscore-prefixed keys (_note, _owner) so operators can comment inline. defaults.claude_tier informs _detect_claude_tier (F003) so the cap-key tier and the v2 vendors{} block tier match without a separate config.

features.description: Claude calibration command + sticky storage. CLI: `python -m jarvis_orchestrate calibrate-claude --dashboard-pct N [--window rolling_7d|rolling_5h]` (default rolling_7d). Reads observed_native for the named window from current ~/.jarvis/quota_state.json. Computes ratio = dashboard_pct / observed_native. Writes the calibration to a SEPARATE sticky file at ~/.jarvis/quota_calibration.json (NOT in-place mutation of quota_state.json — that file is generated state, overwritten on every quota_check.py refresh; calibration is operator configuration that must survive refreshes). Sticky shape: {schema_version: 1, claude: {<window>: {ratio, confidence:'manual', source:'operator_dashboard_sample', dashboard_pct, observed_native, stamped_at}}}. quota_check._build_state lazy-imports calibration_loader.load() (fail-soft, returns {} on any missing/malformed input) and merges matching block into vendors.claude.windows.<window>.calibration via get_for_window which projects to the breaker shape (ratio/confidence/source/stamped_at — drops dashboard_pct + observed_native operator-input metadata). When no sticky entry exists, the uncalibrated default block (ratio:null, confidence:'uncalibrated', source:null, stamped_at:null) is preserved. Confidence levels: uncalibrated (default), manual (this command's output), auto (RESERVED — never set automatically; would require a vendor API that does not exist for the consumer Max plan). Guardrails: dashboard_pct must be in (0, 100], observed_native must be positive (rejects zero), --window restricted to {rolling_7d, rolling_5h} (Claude has no 24h window). quota_check.py main() emits stderr warning when any Claude calibration is older than 7 days (STALE_WARNING_DAYS); operator owns re-cal cadence. Aged calibration still applies (no auto-revert) — warning prompts re-sample.

features.description: Split into F006a (check_budget_ceiling rewrite — done; this entry's evidence_refs document the slice) and F006b (supervisor._quota_gate + quota_admission migrations — pending; passes flips to true only after F006b lands). signoff_writer was originally listed as a third sibling consumer but the F006a design pass surfaced that its `quota_consumed.percent_weekly` is an audit-record field on the audit schema, NOT the quota_state.json legacy mirror — different schema, different concern; descoped accordingly. F006a contract: check_budget_ceiling reads state.vendors[agent].windows; looks up cap+unit via quota_caps_loader.get(vendor, tier, window); applies F005 calibration ratio for Claude windows; returns BudgetCeilingResult with kind ∈ {OK, TRIPPED, CONFIG_REQUIRED, CALIBRATION_REQUIRED, UNIT_MISMATCH}. Function is intentionally pure w.r.t. INBOX writes — caller routes on .kind to emit specific INBOX events (deferred to F006b in the supervisor). Calibration-safety rule: percent_of_plan cap + non-manual confidence → CALIBRATION_REQUIRED halt (NOT a quiet skip; NOT a false-trip against weighted_tokens / 100). Unit-mismatch rule: non-Claude vendor cap.unit ≠ observed_unit → UNIT_MISMATCH halt. Missing/invalid caps file → CONFIG_REQUIRED halt with init guidance. _warned_once dedup keyed by (consumer, agent, condition) and reset between tests via reset_warning_cache(). Legacy fallback (vendors{} missing) uses models{}.percent_weekly + plan.quota_caps with single-shot deprecation log; v2 path IGNORES plan.quota_caps entirely (D010 + F006a operator decision: those values are tied to the broken percent_weekly model and would reintroduce the bug). F006b migrates supervisor._quota_gate (soft-warn at 90% of operator cap, skip uncalibrated Claude, surface 'unmetered/config_required' when no usable window) + quota_admission.evaluate_quota_threshold (defer at >70% of operator cap, prefer rolling_5h primary). Both keep legacy fallback active per F002 mirror policy.
